decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1 to 1-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate despite hurricane-related disruptions.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its assessment to reflect that the economy continues to grow at a solid pace even after recent storms.

changes.quote: Although the hurricanes caused a drop in payroll employment in September, the unemployment rate declined further.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted that storms caused a temporary drop in job additions while unemployment still fell.

changes.quote: Gasoline prices rose in the aftermath of the hurricanes, boosting overall inflation in September; however, inflation for items other than food and energy remained soft.
changes.explanation: Higher gas prices from storm disruptions pushed up headline inflation temporarily, but core inflation stayed weak.

changes.quote: The balance sheet normalization program initiated in October 2017 is proceeding.
changes.explanation: The Fed added an update confirming that its plan to gradually reduce its bond holdings is underway.

changes.quote: Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Janet L. Yellen, Chair; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Lael Brainard; Charles L. Evans; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Jerome H. Powell; and Randal K. Quarles.
changes.explanation: Randal K. Quarles joined the voting members in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting some further strengthening in labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation.

The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant gradual increases in the federal funds rate; the federal funds rate is likely to remain, for some time, below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.77% APR costs about $53.21 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.37% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.88% would fall by about $1.72 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.3%, and employers added an average of 142k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.2% over the past year (September 2017); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.16%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.01% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Committee expects to make gradual increases in the federal funds rate going forward as the economy continues to expand.

citations.detail: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1 to 1-1/4 percent.
